content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4 (full response): the only option that reaches the 80% target, at 88.2% predicted service level for ₹7,575.","why":"The spike is driven by the UPI switch P1 incident (INC-20261006-6998). 213 payments calls arrived at 10:30 against 111.9 forecast, and upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so this is a demand problem, not a people problem. P4 tackles both sides. The IVR outage message and 20% chat deflection cut the incoming load. Moving 4 cross-skilled agents and offering overtime to 40 payments agents (11:15-12:45) add capacity. It also delays payments breaks and cancels coaching. Predicted results are payments 88.1% and general 88.5%, with abandons falling from 9.0% under no action to 3.1%. It breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["Cost: P4 is the most expensive at ₹7,575. P2 costs ₹555 and P3 costs ₹5,475, but they reach only 78.6% and 77.3%, both short of the 80% target.","P2 is the closest cheaper option and handles the outage with messaging. Payments would still sit at 74.2% with 5.3% abandons.","Risk to general: moving 4 agents on its own (P1) would drop general to 37% and breach the MOV-03 floor. In P4 the overtime covers this, and general stays at 88.5% predicted.","Doing nothing (P0) leaves payments at 63.8% and abandons at 9.0%."],"watch":"Overtime uptake: the forecast assumes 40 agents accept from 11:15. If uptake is low, general may suffer from the move, so check that general stays above the 70% floor. Track the UPI incident and stand down the outage message, overtime and the agent move early once the incident is resolved. No escalation is flagged."}
